question: What fish evidence can be independently supported for the Pasig River behind the PMRCIP Phase II/III summaries, and can the cited Phase II completion report be accessed?

exactSearchTerms: Completion Report, Environmental Monitoring and Management PMRCIP Phase II
Completion Report PMRCIP Phase II environmental
searchScope.result: No copy of the specifically cited 2013 Phase II environmental-monitoring completion report was located through these bounded public JICA searches. The JICA/DPWH-hosted 2018 Phase IV EIS reproduces aggregate richness and a separate narrative fish list attributed to it.
searchScope.limit: This records only the searched public routes; it does not establish that the report is unavailable from every source or by request.

independentPrimaryStudy.citation: Chavez, J. M., De La Paz, R. M., Manohar, S. K., Pagulayan, R. C., & Carandang, J. R. (2006). New Philippine record of South American sailfin catfishes (Pisces: Loricariidae). Zootaxa, 1109, 57–68. https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.1109.1.6.
independentPrimaryStudy.studyDesign: Peer-reviewed taxonomic and biogeographic study of 193 examined Pterygoplichthys specimens from five named Laguna de Bay-basin sites.
independentPrimaryStudy.siteAsReported: Pasig River, City of Manila; distinct from the separately named Marikina River site.
independentPrimaryStudy.pasigTaxonAsReported: Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus only; P. pardalis is reported from other study sites but not from the Pasig site.
independentPrimaryStudy.methodsAsReported: Pasig River fish were hand-caught. The authors describe the river sites as medium-velocity and no more than two metres deep near the banks; all fish were caught during daytime. The study examined meristic and morphometric characters and external coloration, and its acknowledgements say external taxonomic experts verified identifications.
independentPrimaryStudy.collectionCatalogContext: The methods identify DLSU ZC-F as the De La Salle University Zoological Collection–Fishes catalog abbreviation, but the reviewed article does not print a Pasig-specific catalog number, date, coordinate, or site-specific specimen count. Figure specimen accession numbers refer to Laguna de Bay, not the Pasig site.
independentPrimaryStudy.evidenceValue: Independent historical, site-named taxonomic evidence for P. disjunctivus at the Manila Pasig River study site. It is not a current observation and does not identify the fish in the separate 2011 EIS claim.
unreportedOrUnresolved: Exact collection date or date range for the Pasig specimens.
Pasig-specific catalog/voucher identifiers, count, and coordinates.
Any direct crosswalk to a PMRCIP Phase II station or the 2011 EIS fish paragraph.

phaseIISecondarySummary.locator: 2018 Supplemental EIS, printed pp. 113–114, Section 6.3.6 and Table 6.3.17.
phaseIISecondarySummary.underlyingSourceAsCited: Completion Report, Environmental Monitoring and Management, PMRCIP, Phase II, 2013.
narrativeTaxonLabelsAsReported: Chitala ornata (printed with the common-name typo ‘Kinife fish’)
phaseIISecondarySummary.limit: The EIS places the narrative under its Phase II secondary-data discussion and says P. disjunctivus is dominant and other fishes inhabit the Pasig River, but does not assign the named taxa to sampling periods, stations, methods, counts, vouchers, or coordinates. Do not copy the names onto each date or infer five dated occurrences from this narrative.

separatePhaseIIIContext.locator: 2018 Supplemental EIS, printed p. 115, Phase III secondary survey discussion and Figure 6.3.14 caption.
separatePhaseIIIContext.resultAsReported: The EIS says only Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus was identified during the survey; Chitala ‘ornate’ (source spelling), Glossogobius giuris, and Arius manilensis are described as supposedly inhabiting and often caught in the river.
separatePhaseIIIContext.limit: Keep this distinct from Phase II counts and species narrative, from the 2006 taxonomic study, and from the 2014 Marikina Bridge survey. The ‘supposedly’ listed fishes are not confirmed identifications from this Phase III survey.

conflicting2011Claim.limit: The 2011 EIS gives no fish-specific date, gear, effort, count, station-by-sample data, or voucher. The 2006 study and 2018 EIS use a Pterygoplichthys label in separate source contexts; they do not prove the 2011 claim refers to the same event or specimen and cannot resolve that identification conflict.

gbifDatasetCheck.interpretation: The Plazi/GBIF entry is a CC0 checklist registration, not a Pasig site-resolved occurrence dataset; the dataset-filtered occurrence API returned zero records. That is a dataset query result only, not biological absence from Pasig or the Philippines. The GBIF metadata license does not grant reuse rights to the underlying Magnolia Press article, figures, or images.

rightsDecision.gbifChecklistDatasetMetadataLicense: CC0 1.0 reported by GBIF API for the registered dataset item; not treated as a license for the copyrighted article.
rightsDecision.decision: Keep attributed summaries and source locators in internal research records. Do not reproduce paper/EIS figures, photos, tables, or long text; no public species row or derived occurrence is approved.

evidenceDecision.historicalSiteTaxonLeadResolved: Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus at the 2006 paper’s named Manila Pasig River study site, as reported by the peer-reviewed study.
evidenceDecision.reason: The primary 2006 study supports one historical named-site taxon but omits its Pasig collection date and specimen IDs. Phase II EIS taxa are not crosswalked to dates or stations; the cited 2013 completion report was not located through the searched public JICA routes. This does not resolve the separate 2011 Ancistrus claim.

nextActions: Seek the 2013 Phase II environmental-monitoring completion report or a preserved copy through the named report authors or project library; request the Pasig station-by-date taxon matrix, methods, effort, and voucher ledger.
If the DLSU ZC-F collection catalog is publicly searchable, seek the Pasig Pterygoplichthys specimen records and collection dates; do not assume generic catalog codes identify specific Pasig lots.
Continue NCR source discovery across freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland waters; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: Peer-reviewed 2006 taxonomic study: five Laguna de Bay-basin sites including Pasig River in Manila; only P. disjunctivus reported at Pasig; collection method and identification context; no Pasig date, specific voucher, site count, or coordinates.
Official 2018 DPWH EIS: Phase II fish-richness counts and narrative taxa list, separate Phase III fish findings, and citation for the underlying Phase II completion report.
Separate undated 2011 EIS Ancistrus/janitor-fish claim; event and specimen remain unresolved.
GBIF dataset API reports CHECKLIST type and CC0 dataset license; dataset-key occurrence API query returned count zero.
